source: OECD (2025), Health at a Glance 2025: OECD Indicators, OECD Publishing, Paris
framing: Gap framing: every figure is what is NOT covered, NOT satisfied or unmet. Gap figures are 100 minus the published figure.
rule: HAL may phrase these facts freely but must not state any figure, ranking or claim that is not in this list. Verbatim report sentences may name other countries; only what they say about this country may be used.

facts.text: 44% of people in Mexico were NOT satisfied with the availability of quality healthcare where they live in 2024, versus an OECD average of 36%.
Population coverage for core services remained below 95% in four OECD countries in 2024, and was below 90% in Mexico and accession country Romania.
In Mexico, the Slovak Republic and Poland, pharmaceuticals accounted for over 60% of OOP spending.
In 2023, the average number of annual in-person doctor consultations per person among OECD countries ranged from fewer than 3 in Mexico, Costa Rica, Sweden and Greece to 18 in Korea (Figure 5.16).
Such countries tend to have higher consultation rates than those countries where doctors are mainly paid by salaries or capitation (such as Denmark, Finland, Mexico and Sweden).
In contrast, Mexico and Costa Rica report the lowest volumes, at around one-fifth of the average.
Households had to bear more than one-third of all healthcare costs directly in Mexico, Chile, Latvia and Greece.
Spending on general outpatient care provided by ambulatory providers was particularly high in Costa Rica, Poland and Mexico, reaching up to 14% of overall health spending.
This compares with the Netherlands, Costa Rica, Mexico, Poland and the United Kingdom where dental care spending represents only around 3% of total health spending.
On the other hand, Canada, Germany and Mexico spent less than 30% of the total health budget on hospitals.

Overall, every third health dollar was spent on ambulatory providers in Belgium, Mexico, Finland, Luxembourg and the United States but this share was below 20% in Türkiye, Greece and the Slovak Republic.
